declarations.name: Rotate
behavior_contract: Positive angles rotate counter-clockwise about the origin.
The source vector is not modified; the operation returns a new value.
The operation is allocation-free and O(1); it is a value operation on the fixed-size record.
Rotate(0) returns a vector equal to the source within ordinary Double comparison.

Rotate(Pi / 2) is consistent with TVector2D.Perpendicular up to a stated 1e-15 relative tolerance; negative angles rotate clockwise and Rotate(-a) is the inverse of Rotate(a) within the same tolerance.
The returned magnitude preserves the source magnitude within the stated tolerance for finite inputs.
Assigning the result back to the source variable (V := V.Rotate(a)) is an ordinary value assignment and is safe.
Rotating the zero vector returns the zero vector exactly.

Non-finite input behavior follows the existing TVector2D contract: non-finite angle or non-finite components propagate the documented non-finite convention of GeometryLib instead of inventing a new one.
The method is documented as thread-safe and reentrant because it reads its value receiver and returns a new value.
test_plan: Compile-check the exact signature against the shipped GeometryLib.Geometry interface and the 1.9 API snapshot diff.
Orientation fixtures: Rotate(Pi / 2) of (1, 0) yields a vector equal to (0, 1) within 1e-15; Rotate(Pi) yields (-1, 0); Rotate(3*Pi/2) yields (0, -1).
Angle conventions: zero angle is identity; negative angle inverts the positive angle of the same magnitude; angle reduction beyond 2*Pi is tested for periodicity consistency.
Perpendicular agreement: Rotate(Pi / 2) is compared with TVector2D.Perpendicular on several ordinary vectors.
Magnitude preservation: relative magnitude deviation is bounded by the stated tolerance for representative vectors including very small and very large finite components.
Source immutability: the receiver record is unchanged after the call, including when the result is assigned back to the same variable.
Zero-vector behavior: Rotate of the zero vector returns the exact zero vector for ordinary angles.
Non-finite policy: NaN or Infinity angle or components follow the documented GeometryLib non-finite contract and are covered by explicit fixtures.
The regression suite runs in normal, optimized, runtime-checked, and heap-traced test builds; allocation freedom is asserted by the heap-traced run and by the fixed-size record contract.
Public-API smoke coverage and the API snapshot reference are updated in the same change.
documentation_plan: Document the exact signature, radians unit, counter-clockwise convention, magnitude tolerance, zero-vector, and non-finite contract in the GeometryLib reference.
Extend the runnable geometry example with a compact rotation workflow whose output is checked by the example-output gate.
Add a recipe or selection note where vector rotation is a common geometry task.
Record the exact addition in the 1.10.0 release notes, API snapshot diff, and capability inventory.
Update the 2.0 candidate snapshot and migration notes to name the new method.

No 1.9.x release may add the declaration; it is declared only by 1.10.0.

deferrals.proposal: Ergonomic 3-D vector rotation (axis-angle, quaternion, or matrix semantics)
deferrals.reason: The closed 1.10.0 manifest adds only the 2-D allocation-free rotation whose design was completed. 3-D rotation still requires a decision among axis-angle, quaternion, and matrix semantics plus orientation, units, normalization, and naming; it is explicitly deferred rather than left open.

deferrals.proposal: Bessel, elliptic, and exponential-integral scalar families
deferrals.reason: No stable public implementation and no demonstrated downstream requirement during 1.9.x convergence; the capability inventory keeps the families visible as unsupported.

deferrals.proposal: Fill-reducing symbolic ordering, multifrontal/supernodal, distributed, out-of-core, and GPU sparse direct algorithms
deferrals.reason: Requires separate storage and performance design beyond the 1.9 stable sparse boundary.

deferrals.proposal: Block/flexible Krylov variants, algebraic multigrid, and parallel/SIMD sparse dispatch
deferrals.reason: No demonstrated need during convergence and no stable parallelism design; portable serial solvers remain the documented path.

deferrals.proposal: Full nonsymmetric, generalized, polynomial, Schur, shift-invert, and interior-target eigensystems
deferrals.reason: The 1.9 stable boundary is full symmetric/Hermitian plus largest-magnitude partial eigensolvers; the remaining families need a dedicated design.

deferrals.proposal: Equiripple and advanced IIR design families and wavelet packets
deferrals.reason: Conditional capability with no qualified numerical validation during convergence; Haar and the shipped filter baselines remain the stable boundary.

deferrals.proposal: Survival analysis, factor analysis, robust covariance, multinomial/count GLMs, boosting, and broader forecasting
deferrals.reason: Not activated because prerequisite numerical validation was not available; visible as unsupported in the capability inventory.

deferrals.proposal: Decomposition, forest, graph, and multivariate-state persistence
deferrals.reason: Selected model adapters are stable; general persistence needs its own interchange design.

deferrals.proposal: Stable thread-pool and SIMD numerical dispatch
deferrals.reason: No stable parallelism API design exists; portable serial oracles remain the 1.x contract.

deferrals.proposal: Any additional domain or algorithm family not shipped in 1.9.x
deferrals.reason: New domains require the GOVERNANCE.md contribution gate: demonstrated user need, a design record, and independent numerical references before implementation.

release_discipline.source_compatibility: Full 1.x source compatibility is retained throughout 1.10.0; no maintained declaration is removed or deprecated.
release_discipline.scope_lock: 1.10.0 implements only the closed declarations above plus the exact documentation, snapshot-diff, migration, and release-candidate work listed in the 1.10.0 roadmap section.
release_candidates: At least two 2.0 release-candidate cycles run from tagged source and offline-documentation archives after the 1.10.0 additions land.
After the freeze, only release-blocking correctness, safety, portability, packaging, documentation, or migration fixes are accepted, each with regression evidence and a reviewed API diff.
Each candidate is exercised through repeated clean-archive representative workflows; elapsed time or an untested artifact is not qualification evidence.
completion_gate: The shipped 1.10.0 public API exactly matches this closed manifest and every addition has a documented contract, focused regression coverage, and a runnable example.
Two release candidates pass full archive-based qualification and the later candidate includes every accepted freeze fix.
No unresolved critical/high-impact correctness, unsafe ownership/concurrency, portability, packaging, or migration defect is hidden to meet the version target.
Representative 1.x applications complete the documented migration or remain operational through the tested compatibility surface.
The only remaining work for 2.0.0 is version/release metadata and promotion of the qualified candidate.
